explainedBy: A traveler heads out to a far planet in the old empire; the compass shows the journey.

storyboard.claim: Malow travels to Sennena deep in the old empire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass icon with the planet name written beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the contrast scene after the generator comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the journey is shown only as a compass and a name.

explainedBy: An old scholar stands in a shabby home.

storyboard.claim: Malow stands in the broken-down home of the old patrician Onum Bar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A thin rumpled old scholar stands beside a house icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Now inside the planet scene: the home and its owner.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the owner as a poor old scholar in a house.

explainedBy: The shield is on, then switched off and its glow vanishes in front of the old scholar.

storyboard.claim: Malow wears a personal force shield, turns it off and the aura vanishes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon beside the old scholar, labeled as turned off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same home, same old man; the shield object is added.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield is the thing that changes; weak: the vanishing glow is text-labeled.

callout.text: Pirenne is stunned by the shield

explainedBy: The man of the empire reacts with shock at the shield.

storyboard.claim: Onum Bar is stunned by the force shield.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The old scholar, wide-eyed, pointing at the shield icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; his face and arm change to astonishment.
storyboard.addedInformation: His reaction to the shield.

explainedBy: The shield stays on screen as the thing the empire never invented at its height.

storyboard.claim: The Empire never invented a personal shield, even at its height.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shield icon alone with the words never invented.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reaction ends; the shield alone carries the claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the negation is carried by text.

explainedBy: The official of a great power stands bowed, the picture of decline rather than explosions.

storyboard.claim: Decay is not always explosions, hordes and fires.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stern heavy-set official standing bowed with a worried face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the shield story to the general lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mood of decline only.

callout.text: Forgetting how your own world works

explainedBy: Time running out stands for a world forgetting itself while a new one is built elsewhere.

storyboard.claim: The tragedy is forgetting how your own world works while someone ignored builds a new one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass icon with the callout.
storyboard.onScreenText: Forgetting how your own world works
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the lesson with the quiet kind of decay.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: icon is symbolic; text carries the point.

explainedBy: An empire official holds a wrench: keeping machines running without understanding them.

storyboard.claim: The Empire has ships and cities but only maintains technology it no longer understands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The heavy-set official with a blank face holding a wrench.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the hollow Empire a person with a tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wrench shows maintenance without comprehension.

explainedBy: The tech expert goes red and threatens arrest when shown the generator.

storyboard.claim: The Trantor-trained tech man turns red and threatens to arrest Malow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The official, angry, pointing accusingly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The expert reacts to the generator.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry accusing expert.

explainedBy: The expert holds up a hand and refuses because he cannot understand.

storyboard.claim: He refuses to believe it is real because he cannot understand it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same official raising a hand in refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man; the action changes from accusing to refusing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Refusal as a gesture.

callout.text: One burnt tube and they are helpless

explainedBy: The caretaker holds his wrench, frightened, helpless in front of a broken machine.

storyboard.claim: The experts are hereditary caretakers who would be helpless if one tube burnt out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same official, afraid, gripping the wrench.
storyboard.onScreenText: Helpless if a single vacuum tube burnt out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man; face changes to fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: The helplessness of a caretaker.

explainedBy: The hosts defend the Empire: a flow begins with years of peace.

storyboard.claim: The Empire kept the peace for years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram with one box: kept the peace.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A host pushes back on the harsh view.
storyboard.addedInformation: Starts the defense as a built chain.

explainedBy: Peace leads to an unimaginable span of stability.

storyboard.claim: The long peace is an unimaginable span of stability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains a second box: stability.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One label is added to the same flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the result of peace.

explainedBy: Massive stability forces maintenance over innovation to prevent collapse.

storyboard.claim: A system that massive prioritizes maintenance over innovation to prevent collapse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains a third box: maintenance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The last label completes the chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the cause chain of the defense.

explainedBy: The counter-host calls the Empire a rotting tree trunk, shown as a tree.

storyboard.claim: No sympathy for the empire: it is a rotting tree trunk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the defense with a new image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree is the image the next beats keep.

explainedBy: Seldon, at his trial, describes the tree: strong bark, hollow inside.

storyboard.claim: Seldon says it looks strong with thick bark but the inside is hollow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon in his wheelchair speaking beside the tree icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same tree; Seldon is added as the speaker.
storyboard.addedInformation: Attributes the image to Seldon.

explainedBy: The sturdy-looking tree gives way when the storm comes, while the Foundation only waits.

storyboard.claim: It looks sturdy until the storm hits; the Foundation just lets the empire collapse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A storm icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The storm replaces the tree as the thing that tests it.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the storm stands in for the coming collapse.

explainedBy: The Empire lacks technicians and fears disruption, so it restricts nuclear power.

storyboard.claim: The Empire restricts nuclear power because it lacks technicians and fears disruption.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: lack technicians leads to restricted nuclear power.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the scarcity versus abundance comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Empire side of the cause chain.

explainedBy: The Foundation, short of metal, shrinks nuclear tech into walnut generators.

storyboard.claim: Stranded on a metal-starved rock, the Foundation miniaturizes nuclear tech.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A new flow: starved for metal leads to walnut generators.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new flow for the Foundation side after the Empire flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Foundation side of the comparison.

explainedBy: Scarcity versus abundance: one drove innovation, the other bred stagnation.

storyboard.claim: Scarcity drove innovation while immense abundance bred fatal stagnation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum with the poles scarcity and abundance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the two flows as two poles.
storyboard.addedInformation: The summary contrast on one scale.

explainedBy: The Empire clings to decaying ships; the hourglass shows time running out.

storyboard.claim: The Empire clings to massive decaying ships and forgotten science, slowly dying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the comparison with the Empire fate.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-led.

explainedBy: The official sags, acting inside a fate he refuses to face.

storyboard.claim: The Empire acts inside a historical inevitability it refuses to accept.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The heavy-set official, bowed and worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the Empire a bowed figure for its fate.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mood only.

explainedBy: The hosts turn to a structural criticism of the universe.

storyboard.claim: We must level an honest structural criticism: the human element.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon talking, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new topic: the criticism of the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: commentary.

explainedBy: The story is driven by a few elite men: a mayor and a scholar stand in front.

storyboard.claim: Psychohistory treats people as numbers and the story is driven by elite men.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mayor and a scholar pointing out, both with smirks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the elite men the narration names.
storyboard.addedInformation: The elite men are on screen.

explainedBy: Masses are manipulated by great men: a puppeteer controlling others.

storyboard.claim: Women and ordinary people barely get agency; the masses are a tide manipulated by great men.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the elite men to what they do to the masses.
storyboard.addedInformation: The control relation.

explainedBy: Even a brilliant anomaly like the Mule leaves the story cold and controlled.

storyboard.claim: The sheer scale can make the narrative feel cold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The puppeteer icon kept.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout changes.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-led.

explainedBy: The math is a magical shield protecting the author preferred outcome.

storyboard.claim: The math is a magical shield protecting the author preferred outcome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new image for the convenient revelation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield stands for the protecting math.

explainedBy: Seldon smirks: the Second Foundation ensures he is always right.

storyboard.claim: The Second Foundation is a narrative cheat code so Seldon is always right.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon smirking in his wheelchair.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Seldon is shown as the one who wins.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk marks the rigged win.

explainedBy: The hosts list the topics covered.
noVisual: A recap of four earlier topics: no single picture shows the list.

storyboard.claim: After the holograms, nuclear priests, economic warfare and decaying empires, what does it mean?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The words only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: recap, text only.

explainedBy: The mayor stands plainly: the thesis says he is not a hero.

storyboard.claim: Foundation is not about heroes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The mayor standing neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the hero shown plain.

callout.text: A massive crowd steered by math

explainedBy: A massive crowd is steered by math: the puppeteer.

storyboard.claim: It is about a massive crowd steered by math.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon with the callout.
storyboard.onScreenText: A massive crowd steered by math
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The control relation again.

explainedBy: Seldon, who made the plan, smirks that the people inside must not know it exists.

storyboard.claim: The plan survives only because the people inside do not know it exists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon smirking and speaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The irony lands.
storyboard.addedInformation: The planner who hides it.

explainedBy: The hosts address the viewer.
noVisual: The listener is addressed directly; no person in the cast is the listener.

storyboard.claim: Ask yourself a deeply uncomfortable question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The words only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves to the closing address.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: direct address, text only.

explainedBy: Forces swirling around you control your choices.

storyboard.claim: How many of your choices are yours and how many the result of forces?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon with the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the question with the control image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The control image applied to the viewer.

explainedBy: Are you the driver or just a predictable number?

storyboard.claim: Are you the driver of your life or just another predictable number?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The puppeteer kept with the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the final line.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: ends on a question, text-led.
